To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ethylene is an important gaseous hormone in plants, that it is synthesized via ACC and that the ethylene signal is transduced via the ethylene receptor.
ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone that regulates a multitude of physiological processes.

ethylene biosynthesis is controlled at the level of ACC synthase gene expression and that ethylene signal transductions is controlled by a MAP kinase cascade, in which the ethylene receptors are negative regulators.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the molecular basis of ethylene biosynthesis and signal transduction in plants, with an emphasis on the role of ACC synthase in ethylene synthesis and on ethylene receptors in signal perception.
the identification, characterization and manipulation of ethylene biosynthesis and ethylene response genes.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms of ethylene biosynthesis, perception, signal transduction and gene regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ethylene is a signal molecule that is perceived by receptors, transduced through CTR1, EIN2, and EIN3, and finally results in the activation of ethylene responsive promoters.
ethylene is a plant hormone which is produced in response to a variety of environmental and endogenous signals.
Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone that regulates a multitude of developmental processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to show that the ethylene receptor is the target for a signal that is transduced by a protein kinase, CTR1, that is related to Raf.
the molecular basis of the ethylene pathway has been identified and characterized.
the ethylene receptor is a negative regulator of ethylene signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ethylene is not only a ripening hormone, it is also an important regulator of plant development.
ethylene is a gaseous molecule that can diffuse freely in the air, so it is not surprising that it can be used as a signal molecule.
the ethylene receptor is a negative regulator of ethylene responses and that ethylene sensitivity can be modulated by genetic modification of the receptor gene.
